slice.probe: Test the current scheduled-Chat-exposed single-ref transaction-record protocol: encode logical state, prior-link, idempotency key and witness metadata in one Git commit, then advance exactly one mutable branch ref with force=false. Model W1/W2 from a common head, exact and semantic duplicate replay, and a force-capable rewind; classify which failure classes disappear and whether rollback evidence is independently recoverable without protected/admin authority, manual execution, or finite quota.

source_refs.claim: GitHub's Update a reference endpoint points one ref at a SHA; force omitted/false enforces a fast-forward update and avoids overwriting work.
GitHub exposes creation of a Git commit from a tree plus parent commit SHAs.
GitHub exposes creation of a tree from explicit entries and an optional base tree.

The current GitHub connector exposes create_blob, create_tree, create_commit, fetch/fetch_commit/fetch_blob, and singular update_ref with force default false, so the single-ref protocol is callable from scheduled Chat without GraphQL, hosted compute, or a manual executor.

protocol_record.advance_rule: create immutable blob/tree/commit with parent=current tip; reread/verify expected current tip as needed; call update_ref(force=false) only when the transaction/idempotency key is not already represented in current state

model.stale_sibling_result: If W1 advances C0->C1 first, C2 is not a descendant of C1. A subsequent force=false ref update to C2 is non-fast-forward and is rejected, so the stale sibling does not become committed protocol state.
model.exact_duplicate_replay: If the same candidate C1/tx-1 is replayed after the ref already equals C1, a read-before-write equality check makes the operation a protocol no-op. The protocol does not depend on undocumented behavior for an update-to-identical-SHA call.
model.semantic_duplicate_from_old_parent: A newly constructed duplicate C1_prime carrying tx-1 but parent C0 is a stale sibling after C1 and is rejected by force=false. This blocks duplicate durable state even if the commit SHA differs because of metadata/timestamps.
model.semantic_duplicate_from_current_parent: A newly constructed tx-1 duplicate on top of C1 would be a valid fast-forward, so fast-forward alone is insufficient for idempotency. The current transaction record must carry transaction_id/idempotency_key state, and the writer must reject an already-recorded key before constructing/advancing another commit.

force_capable_actor.result: A force-capable actor can rewind the sole mutable ref to an older valid commit. The branch tip and its internally cross-linked record then expose only the older chain; the removed newer transaction cannot be inferred from that ref alone.

failure_classification.partial_state_vs_witness_commit: eliminated_when_both are encoded in the same committed tree/commit
failure_classification.prepared_but_uncommitted_object: possible but not protocol-visible; a commit object may be created before a failed ref advance and remain unreachable
failure_classification.stale_sibling_commit: eliminated_for_compliant writers by force=false fast-forward enforcement
failure_classification.semantic_duplicate_replay: requires transaction-id/idempotency-key membership in the committed state; fast-forward enforcement alone is insufficient

rollback_evidence_analysis: The transaction hash chain is self-authenticating only relative to the currently reachable tip. After a coherent force rewind, the older tip is internally valid and contains no evidence that a later transaction once existed.

An unreachable commit might remain retrievable by a previously known SHA, but a scheduled cross-run protocol cannot rely on ephemeral knowledge of that SHA, and no durable retention guarantee for unreachable objects was established as an independently monotonic witness.

Persisting the newer SHA in another mutable ref or same-authority repository file restores a second witness location but not an independently monotonic authority; a force-capable same-authority actor can coherently rewind both.

Branch protection/rules, administrative audit authority, a separately controlled witness, manual attestation, or external retained storage could strengthen rollback evidence, but each introduces protected/admin/manual/external-authority assumptions outside the current accepted zero-residual-dependency route unless independently eliminated.
findings: Unlike the prior GraphQL updateRefs candidate, every primitive needed for the single-ref commit-and-advance path is exposed in the current scheduled-Chat GitHub connector.
Collapsing logical state and witness metadata into one immutable commit and using one mutable ref removes the multi-ref torn-update class rather than merely narrowing its window.
force=false provides a useful concurrency gate but is not a complete idempotency mechanism; transaction identity must be part of the committed state.

The protocol remains fail-closed for full Phase-1 acceptance because a same-authority force rewind can erase branch-visible knowledge of a newer transaction and no independently monotonic rollback witness has been established within the zero-protected/zero-manual/zero-finite-quota constraints.
slice.tested_scope: One bounded CLEAN protocol/concurrency model using public GitHub Git-database/ref semantics and current connector capability discovery: one mutable ref, immutable commit record, W1/W2 common-parent contention, exact and semantic duplicate replay, and one force-capable rewind. No live protocol-branch mutation, O/downstream/other-worker semantic input, protected/admin mutation, hosted compute/storage add-on, external model/API execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, manual execution, scheduler mutation, same-run retry, or optional second leaf.
slice.conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child; frozen exact authority remained valid, own LATEST was unchanged at r272 before mutation, and only own role-local checkpoint/LATEST and immutable own receipt namespaces are mutated.

frontier: The single-ref transaction-record design is current-Chat-callable and removes the separate-ref torn/partial protocol state class.
force=false rejects stale old-parent sibling commits but does not itself reject a semantic duplicate built on the current tip; committed transaction-id state is required.
The remaining decisive gap is not commit atomicity but independently monotonic knowledge that a newer transaction existed before a force-capable coherent rewind.
The unavailable GraphQL multi-ref atomic path remains an alternative, but it shares the same monotonic-witness gap and is no longer the highest-value immediate route.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current controls and reconstruct r273 from LATEST. Execute exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child: test whether any currently Chat-readable GitHub-native provider-controlled event or immutable-object surface can serve as an independently retained rollback witness for the single-ref transaction protocol without branch protection/rules administration, organization audit-log authority, manual attestation, hosted compute/storage, external service execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental cost. Distinguish mere post-hoc object retrievability from a durable monotonic record that a specific newer transaction existed; model force-rewind detection and retention/visibility failure. Preserve the single-ref transaction protocol as the current callable baseline and fail closed if the witness is mutable, permission-gated, retention-limited without durable guarantee, or requires another execution authority.
